# Vento Labs

> Vento Labs is an AI automation agency (Vento Labs Pte. Ltd., registered in Singapore, UEN 202504485G, working remotely from Lisbon). We design and build custom AI agents that cut operating costs, automate workflows, and scale businesses without adding headcount. Every engagement can start with a Digital Business Brain: for $500, we connect a client's databases, CRM, ERP, team chats and kanban boards into one AI layer and surface the insight already hiding in the data.

Key facts:
- Founded: 2025. Founder & lead engineer: Alexey Nagorny (alexey@ventolabs.com).
- Stack: Claude Agent SDK, LangGraph, CrewAI, n8n, Make.com, MCP servers. Self-hosted deployments — client data stays in the client's infrastructure.
- Typical timelines: basic AI agent in 3–7 days; process automation in 1–3 weeks; company-wide AI platform in 2–4 weeks.
- Typical running costs: AI model usage $20–200/month, paid directly to providers with no markup.
- Digital Business Brain: $500 flat, connects a client's existing systems (databases, CRM, ERP, chats, kanban boards) into one AI layer.
- AI Platform pricing: Pilot from $3,000 setup + $500/month; Scale from $8,000 setup + $2,000/month; Enterprise custom.
- Booking: https://cal.com/ventolabs/30min (30-minute discovery call, free).
- Languages: English (default), German (/de/), Spanish (/es/), Russian (/ru/).

## Services

The four services are distinct engagements, in rough order of scope: one agent (ai-assistant) → your tools wired together (ai-automation) → your people trained (ai-training) → the whole company on one platform (ai-workspace).

- [AI Agents](https://ventolabs.com/services/ai-assistant/): One custom AI agent, built for you and self-hosted on your server, VPS or local machine. Built on Claude Agent SDK, LangGraph or CrewAI; any LLM backend including fully local models. Integrates with Telegram, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, email (Gmail/Outlook), Slack and any API; computer-use for browsing, filling forms and extracting data; connects to your docs, FAQ, CRM and databases. Basic agent live in 3–7 days, complex multi-platform builds 1–3 weeks. The usual starting engagement is a $500 Digital Business Brain; production agents are fixed-price quoted after the discovery call.
- [AI Automation](https://ventolabs.com/services/ai-automation/): Workflow automation across the tools you already run, built on n8n (self-hosted, no per-task pricing) and Make.com. Process audit and automation roadmap, AI-powered lead qualification and response drafting, cross-platform data sync (CRM ↔ sheets ↔ email ↔ chat), automated reporting, webhook triggers, error monitoring and alerting, and ongoing maintenance as the connected tools change. AI handles the judgement calls that previously required a person.
- [AI Consulting & Training](https://ventolabs.com/services/ai-training/): Team enablement and consulting. AI maturity assessment, Claude Code and Cursor installed and configured for every developer, MCP servers wired to your tools and databases, custom prompt libraries, hands-on workshops using the team's real work rather than demos, follow-up sessions and adoption measurement at 30 and 60 days, and a best-practices playbook. Also consulting on in-house AI projects: architecture, tool selection, risk assessment.
- [AI Platform](https://ventolabs.com/services/ai-workspace/): Company-wide AI operating system for teams of roughly 5 to 200+. A dedicated agent per function (client service, sales, marketing, operations), an AI assistant with full company context for every employee, a Knowledge Vault indexing all company knowledge, connections to CRM, email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Shopify, Google Drive, Notion, Slack and any REST API, role-based access with audit logs, usage and ROI reporting, and AI-usage policy documentation. Self-hosted, live in 4 weeks. Pricing per the tiers listed above.

## AI infrastructure

- [AI Data Centers](https://ventolabs.com/data-centers/): End-to-end development of AI data centers for investors and owners — deciding what to build, site search, securing land and grid capacity, transmission interconnection, modular construction, commissioning, and operation. Typical projects 10–100+ MW, phased. Modular deployment in 3–6 months against 24–36 for conventional construction; target PUE below 1.3; liquid-cooled racks up to 100 kW. Engagement structures: turnkey build you own, build-to-suit against a signed offtake, or joint venture. Sites currently in diligence or under evaluation in Texas, the US Midwest (MISO), and Sweden. Counterparty names, exact addresses, and commercial terms are not published — the underlying materials are under confidentiality agreements.

## Shipped products

- [ArbitrAI](https://arbitrai.tech/): Vento Labs' own LegalTech product — an AI platform for Russian bankruptcy trustees (deadline control under the insolvency law, AI-drafted filings, transaction analysis). Results: daily deadline monitoring 2–3 hours → under 20 minutes, 99.9% of statutory publications filed on time, document prep 6× faster. Source: Vento Labs' own measurements on the product; not an independent audit.
- [Case studies](https://ventolabs.com/cases/): the four productized solutions below, plus ArbitrAI. Note on evidence: Vento Labs does not publish named client engagements. Figures on the site are either from our own products, or labelled with their source; anything unattributed has been removed rather than presented as a client outcome.

## Product directions

- [Content Factory](https://ventolabs.com/cases/content-factory/): Turns e-commerce catalogs into daily discovery content — lifestyle visuals, carousels, short videos, AI presenters.
- [Supplier Agent](https://ventolabs.com/cases/supplier-agent/): Reads supplier emails, chats and price lists; extracts SKUs, prices, stock; updates catalogs by rules with approval flows.
- [1C Agent](https://ventolabs.com/cases/erp-agent/): An AI developer for 1C, the dominant ERP platform in the Russian-speaking market. The IT director or head of department describes a task in plain business language; the agent returns a change plan and writes it only after that plan is approved. Changes land in configuration extensions, so the standard 1C core is never modified and vendor updates keep working. Full audit log of command, action and result; pilot in 2–4 weeks; self-hosted ready. Russian-market product: the en/de/es URLs are short localized summaries, the full case study is Russian-only at /ru/cases/erp-agent/.
- [Bankruptcy AI](https://ventolabs.com/cases/bankruptcy-agent/): AI platform for Russian arbitration trustees («арбитражные управляющие») working under insolvency law 127-FZ — reports to the creditors' meeting and to the court on the statutory forms, procedural filings citing current Supreme Court practice, statutory deadline control, and debtor transaction analysis across the public registries and bank statements. The platform drafts; the trustee reviews, signs with a qualified electronic signature and files. Self-hosted inside the trustee's own perimeter, NDA before any data is connected; subscription from USD 2,500/month. This is the same solution Vento Labs now also develops as the standalone product ArbitrAI (see Client results above). Russian-market product: the en/de/es URLs are short localized summaries, the full page is Russian-only at /ru/cases/bankruptcy-agent/.

## Engineering guides

Long-form write-ups at https://ventolabs.com/blog/. Each guide is published in one language — the language of the market it serves — and the other three locales carry a summary that links back to the original, not a translation.

- [AI tooling for 1C:Enterprise in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex](https://ventolabs.com/ru/blog/instrumenty-1c-claude-code-codex/) (Russian, ~16 min): survey of the AI tooling around 1C — three dozen MCP servers for metadata, queries and the event log; Claude Code skill packs that generate forms, reports, roles and data composition schemas; the official BSL Language Server plugin; the Unica plugin for OpenAI Codex; 1C:Naparnik. Covers install order, what works in both agents, and why an LLM without MCP writes confident but wrong BSL.
- [An AI agent for 1C: what it can do, where it breaks, how to deploy it safely](https://ventolabs.com/ru/blog/ai-agent-dlya-1c-vnedrenie/) (Russian, ~14 min): the four task classes AI agents genuinely handle on top of 1C (data Q&A, ad-hoc reports, routine operations, developer assistance) and the safe-access architecture — a dedicated user on a read-only role by default, a change plan reviewed by a human before any write, changes confined to configuration extensions so the vendor core stays supported, and a full audit trail. Includes the honest list of areas to keep an AI out of (posting documents unreviewed, period close, statutory reporting) and a 2–4 week rollout.
- [A digital employee for marketplaces: an AI agent for Wildberries and Ozon sellers](https://ventolabs.com/ru/blog/ai-agent-dlya-marketpleysov-wb-ozon/) (Russian, ~14 min): how an agent on the official WB and Ozon Seller APIs takes over seller routine — scheduled ETL into your own database, unit economics computed in code against your real cost of goods, scheduled digests in Telegram, card content and review drafts. Also the honest limits: API rate ceilings, financial-data lag, and areas of the seller dashboard with no API where browser automation breaks on every redesign.
- [AI for bankruptcy trustees: which parts of the procedure an agent can already handle](https://ventolabs.com/ru/blog/ii-dlya-arbitrazhnogo-upravlyayushchego/) (Russian, ~14 min): deadline control under Russian insolvency law (127-FZ), bank statement screening for voidable transactions with affiliation data from the companies register, drafts of reports and statutory publications, court docket monitoring. The boundary is explicit: the agent prepares, the trustee decides and signs — liability is personal and non-delegable.
- [How much does a custom AI agent cost in 2026? An honest breakdown](https://ventolabs.com/blog/custom-ai-agent-cost/) (English, ~14 min): market-wide build ranges (prototype $5–15k; production single-workflow agent $15–50k; multi-system agent $50–150k+) and monthly run cost broken into tokens, hosting, monitoring and a maintenance retainer. The five drivers behind any quote, break-even arithmetic for no-code vs SaaS vs custom, hidden costs, and the cases where you should not build. Figures are public market ranges as of July 2026, not a Vento Labs price list.
- [Autonomous AI without delegating accountability](https://ventolabs.com/blog/autonomous-ai-accountability/) (English, German, Spanish and Russian, ~6 min): you can delegate tasks and decision-making authority to an agent, but not accountability. The five things every deployed agent needs — a written scope of authority, system-enforced limits on data and spend, defined approval points, a complete record of decisions and actions, and one named business owner who can switch it off. Why "human in the loop" is usually not a control, and why a defined boundary makes deployment faster rather than slower.

## Company

- [Home](https://ventolabs.com/): The offer, the process, and the proof. Offer: a Digital Business Brain — one 30-minute call to scope a client's systems, then for $500 we connect their databases, CRM, chats and kanban boards into an AI layer that surfaces the insight already in the data, so the value is visible before anything larger is signed. Process, three phases: Audit — a 30-minute call in which we map the real process and identify where AI saves the most time and money right now; Build — the first agent wired into the existing tools, knowledge base and workflows, working in days rather than months; Scale — automation extended across operations by priority, each iteration against explicit KPIs, with ongoing support. Proof shown on the page: the productized solutions (Content Factory, Supplier Agent, 1C Agent), each linking to its full case; separately, third-party productivity research (Stanford & MIT 2023, Science 2023, GitHub & Microsoft 2022) cited and linked as external evidence, explicitly not presented as our own results. Vento Labs does not publish named third-party client engagements. Also on the page: the four service lines, links to the AI data center practice and the engineering guides, the founder you actually deal with (Alexey Nagorny, founder and lead engineer — there is no sales layer), and a FAQ covering hallucination control, what data leaves the client's infrastructure, monthly running cost, implementation time, whether an engagement can stop after the first setup, and industry fit.

## Machine-readable endpoints

- [Agent card (A2A)](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/agent-card.json): nine delivery skills — the four services, data centers, and the four productized solutions — for agent-to-agent routing.
- [MCP server card](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json): the in-page WebMCP surface (`navigator.modelContext`). A visiting agent can book a consultation or fetch contact details without leaving the page.
- [API catalog (RFC 9727)](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/api-catalog): one entry, the public notify webhook, with its [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/openapi/notify.json) and [human-readable docs](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/api-docs/notify.html).
- [Agent Skills discovery index](https://ventolabs.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): intentionally an empty `skills` array. That index advertises downloadable `SKILL.md` procedure files for an agent to execute; Vento Labs publishes none. It is deliberately NOT a mirror of the nine A2A skills above — those describe work this company delivers, not instructions an agent can run. Do not treat the empty array as an oversight.
